ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Flannery O'Connor — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Six-month response assessment: complete renal response; prednisone 5 mg; pregnancy planning

text.paragraph: Six-month review of lupus nephritis; pregnancy planning. [S]

Ms. O'Connor is six months into treatment. She reached prednisone 5 mg a day a week ago. Her joints and skin remain quiet; she has had no fevers, infections, or hip pain since the summer. Monthly blood counts have been normal. She had her influenza vaccine at the preventive visit three weeks ago. She has finished a draft of her novel. She would like to have children in a few years and asked what that would mean for her treatment. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1950-10-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: No synovitis; full, painless hip movement

Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus at the second visit; joint pain in 1950 with suspected rheumatoid arthritis is documented (D).
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding at the index visit, superseded by the kidney biopsy diagnosis at the third visit.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and results; her systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in Atlanta in late 1950 or early 1951, is documented (D), but no finding from her lifetime is used.

Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class III (A), focal proliferative, on kidney biopsy: endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, full-house immunofluorescence; no thrombotic microangiopathy; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g; normal kidney function
S — Synthetic biopsy result and class; kidney involvement is documented at the end of her life, but no kidney finding from her lifetime is used.
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less
S — Synthetic treatment status; the documented steroid harm in her life is the reason the episode keeps glucocorticoids low.
Long-term mycophenolate mofetil, with belimumab, for lupus nephritis; bone and infection protection in place
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system for highly effective contraception during mycophenolate treatment
S — Synthetic contraception, chosen by the patient.

Acute cystitis on mycophenolate, belimumab, and prednisone 15 mg: two days of burning, frequency, and urgency without fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved with seven days of nitrofurantoin
S — Synthetic common infection in an immunosuppressed young woman; coded without hematuria because the persistent hematuria is from her nephritis.

list.item:
Class III lupus nephritis (M32.14). Complete renal response at six months: protein-to-creatinine ratio 0.35 g/g, red cells 2 per high-power field, creatinine 0.8. Anti-dsDNA 38 and complements normal (C3 96, C4 18). Treatment continues for three to five years after a complete response before any reduction. [S]
Continue mycophenolate, belimumab, hydroxychloroquine, and losartan.
Prednisone 5 mg; withdrawal to be considered after a further period of quiet disease.
Kidney panel, urine protein, and serology every three months.

Pregnancy planning (Z97.5). Pregnancy is possible and safest after at least six months of quiet disease on pregnancy-compatible medicines. Her negative antiphospholipid tests mean no heparin is expected. Lupus nephritis raises the risk of preeclampsia. [S]
When she is ready: switch mycophenolate to azathioprine and stop losartan, with at least six weeks off mycophenolate before trying and a period of stability on azathioprine first.
Continue hydroxychloroquine through pregnancy; belimumab reviewed with her rheumatologist before conception.
Anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies before pregnancy; low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks; joint care with obstetrics.
Keep the intrauterine system until then.

Glucocorticoids: bone (Z79.52). No hip pain; vitamin D replete. [S]
Repeat DXA in one to two years while on glucocorticoids.

list.item: Establish the diagnosis within two weeks and hear it directly, in plain words. Outcome by 1950-04-22: Told directly at nine days that she has systemic lupus erythematosus, with the reasons and a written summary [S]

Renal response: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio halved by three months and below 0.5 g/g with stable kidney function by six to twelve months. Outcome by 1950-10-26: Ratio 1.8 at diagnosis, 0.9 at three months, 0.35 at six months, a complete response; creatinine 0.8 throughout [S]
